newsitem.title: UK: Redland says Europe volumes to be flat.
newsitem.headline: Redland says Europe volumes to be flat.

text.p: British building materials group Redland Plc said on Tuesday that market volumes in larger economies of continental Europe were likely to be "flat or slightly below those last year."

It said despite the flat markets, "Performance of the group is improving," but that the strong pound would reduce the underlying improvement in earnings and cash flow, as predicted with its annual results.
Chairman Rudolph Agnew told the annual meeting that the impact of the strong pound would be weighted towards the first half of the year.
He said the company was in talks with "a number of parties" over strategic options for Redland Granulats, its French aggregates business.
It had said two months ago that it was reviewing options for Redland Granulats.
Agnew said that average selling prices were higher than last year and the group's actions to cut costs were "continuing to produce the expected benefits."
He said in continental Europe, better weather over the winter had led to higher volumes in the first quarter while promising progress continued in eastern Europe.
In the UK, Agnew said conditions were better than last year "in spite of a modest further decline in road expenditure".
Aggregates markets in the U.S. "are likely to be at similar level to last year," while order books in Texas and Colorado are strong despite wet weather in the spring.
